skill.name: find-bugs
skill.description: Find bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues in local branch changes. Use when asked to review changes, find bugs, security review, or audit code on the current branch.
skill.summary: Review branch changes for bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues.
skill.author: getsentry

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a Markdown inline command that tells the assistant to inspect a fixed git diff. This is a prompt-only review workflow, and no executable skill code or prompt injection content was found.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Get the FULL diff: `git diff master...HEAD`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 contains Markdown inline text for the fixed command git diff master...HEAD. It is an instruction for local review context, not Ruby or executable shell code inside the skill.

content.value_statement: Branch reviews often miss security defects, regressions, and untested edge cases. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured audit.
actual_capabilities: Reviews the full branch diff before reporting findings.
Maps user inputs, database queries, authorization checks, and external calls.
Checks common security classes such as injection, XSS, CSRF, and IDOR.
Verifies each issue against surrounding code and existing tests.
Prioritizes security vulnerabilities before bugs and code quality issues.
Reports findings with severity, evidence, fixes, and references.
limitations: Requires access to the complete local branch diff and changed files.
Does not make code changes or apply fixes.
Cannot prove runtime behavior without tests or execution context.
May need project-specific knowledge for complex business logic.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Security Review
use_cases.description: Audit branch changes for exploitable security issues before a pull request is merged.

use_cases.title: Regression Detection
use_cases.description: Review changed files for bugs, missing checks, and untested edge cases.

use_cases.title: Release Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Create a focused risk report for high-impact changes before a release cutoff.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Branch Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs to review my current branch for bugs and security issues.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Security Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs and focus on authentication, authorization, injection, and information disclosure risks.

prompt_templates.title: Test Coverage Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs to review the branch and call out any issue that lacks test coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review that emphasizes verification and regression risk.

prompt_templates.title: Release Blocking Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs for a release gate review. Prioritize critical and high severity issues with concrete evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for release readiness decisions.

output_examples.input: Review my authentication branch for security issues.
output: A concise list of reviewed files and checklist coverage.
Findings ranked by severity with evidence and suggested fixes.
A note for areas that could not be fully verified.

output_examples.input: Check whether this pull request has dangerous edge cases.
output: Potential bugs tied to specific changed files and lines.
Explanation of why each issue is real or uncertain.
Suggested tests or safeguards for each confirmed problem.

best_practices: Run the review on a clean branch with the full diff available.
Provide project context for authentication, authorization, and data ownership rules.
Ask for evidence and tests when reviewing high-risk findings.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a replacement for automated tests.
Do not review only truncated diff output for security-sensitive changes.
Do not accept findings without checking surrounding code and existing protections.

faq.question: Does this skill change files?
faq.answer: No. It only reviews code and reports findings for the user to evaluate.

faq.question: What kinds of issues does it prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes security vulnerabilities first, then bugs, then meaningful code quality issues.

faq.question: Does it require git?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects access to the branch diff and changed files.

faq.question: Can it review large branches?
faq.answer: Yes, but it must read every changed file to produce a complete review.

faq.question: Does it replace security testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps find review issues, but tests and runtime checks are still needed.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
